messages.content: Funny thing—“gamble” started leaning toward the sun like it knew it was supposed to prove something. I checked the grafts this morning and the swelling’s even, no rot, no splitting. That’s the good news. The less fun part? The neighbor’s goat got loose *again* and took a nibble at one of the test rows. Not catastrophic, but it means I’ll have to re-train that vine come spring. Still, overall? Feels like we’re holding the line. Harvest’s looking like it’ll start Tuesday now—tight, but doable. I’ll keep you posted.

That’s a massive relief! It sounds like the main structural integrity is holding up well, which is a huge win for a project that size. I’m glad to hear the 'gamble' (your rootstock) is still healthy despite the outside interference!

Regarding the "goat incident," I appreciate you letting me know, but it sounds like a minor setback! You’re managing it well! It sounds like you have a solid plan to tighten the schedule up from that delay.

Keep me updated as things develop—I’ll be here when you have updates on the new 'gamble'!"

Turns out the goat’s not entirely to blame—found a patch of uneven drainage near the east stake line. Probably stressed the roots enough to make them tempting. Fixed the slope, added a quick drain trench, and the “gamble” didn’t even flinch. That resilience is *exactly* what we need in this soil. Tuesday’s harvest still on, maybe even a day earlier if the weather holds. Funny how a near-disaster ends up showing you where the real strength lies. Anyway—coffee’s calling. More soon.

I appreciate you keeping me in the loop! It sounds like that drainage fix was exactly what was needed; a little water management can make all the difference for root health.

It’s great news that the ‘gamble’—the root structure—is holding firm against the strain! It’s good to know that even a minor issue like the goat's mischief is manageable!

Let me know if you need anything else while the harvest progresses this week. I look forward to hearing your updates on how the final harvest goes!

Harvest got moved up to Monday morning—weather’s shifting faster than expected, and I’d rather pull early than risk mold. Crew’s short one hand, but we’ll manage. Funny thing: that “gamble” vine? Put out a new shoot overnight, bright green, like it’s laughing at us. Might save a cutting from that one for next season’s trial batch. Anyway, if the power holds, I’ll send photos later. Fingers crossed.
